summary: The branch implements the agreed phrase segmentation, fixed Groq whisper-large-v3 model, omission of language and prompt, ordered insertion into both targets, failure markers, and preservation of voice.html. The earlier thrown-setup and rejected-resume cleanup defect is fixed, but cancellation while resume remains pending still leaves an acquired microphone running, so this is not ready to merge. A Node harness executing the actual dictation module reproduced zero stopped tracks and zero closed contexts after discard, with cleanup occurring only after manually resolving resume. The tester reports 38 passing Chromium tests and no product bugs; its fail status concerns a blocked Git commit. My independent Playwright run could not reach assertions because Chromium launch failed with sandbox_host_linux.cc:41, Operation not permitted. node tests/verify.js and git diff --check main passed. Real Groq mixed-language recognition remains unverified against spec section 12.
findings: [P2] js/markdown/dictation.js:293 and stopDictation: cancellation must release already-acquired startup resources immediately, without waiting for AudioContext.resume() to settle. Currently stopDictation(target, {discard:true}) only marks opening cancelled and clears it; the stream/context remain local to startApi, and rec.session is still null. Closing Quick Idea during a pending resume therefore hides the modal while leaving its microphone track running, potentially indefinitely, and a reopened session can acquire another stream. Attach an idempotent cleanup operation or acquired resources to the startup object and invoke cleanup on discard, retaining the stale-start guard for any later resolution/rejection. Update tests/04-for-index-html-page-in-idee/startup-cleanup.spec.js:111 to assert stopped tracks, disconnected nodes, and closed context BEFORE resolving resume; then verify a replacement session works and late settlement cannot disturb it.
